abstract: For high-definition satellite newsgathering (HD-SNG) applications, 4:2:0 video codecs are widely used; however, there is one major draw-back to 4:2:0 chroma sampling. When two or more 4:2:0 codecs are concatenated, the chroma component gradually becomes blurred because the codecs are usually connected via high-definition serial digital interface (HD-SDI) (a 4:2:2 interconnect) resulting in upsampling and downsampling of the chroma component. To solve this problem, a new chroma downsampling and upsampling filter set has been designated for the 4:2:0 codec, whereby chroma degradation is completely suppressed after several stages of concatenation. This paper explains the features of the 4:2:2/4:2:0 perfect reconstruction filter set and discusses its application for HD-SNG.

authors.bio: Akira Nakagawa is a senior researcher in the Audiovisual Systems Laboratory at Fujitsu Laboratories Ltd. He received an M.S. degree from the University of Tokyo in 1991. Nakagawa is engaged in the efficient video coding scheme and architecture of H.261, H.263, MPEG-1, MPEG-2, MPEG-4, and H.264/AVC. He received the “Paper of MoMuC'97 Award” at the International Workshop on Mobile Multimedia Communication MoMuC'97.
